title: Echo Observatory · Operations
description: Curated operational dashboard for Echo Observatory 2.x. Current state, changing rates and selected-period comparisons; standard Grafana and Prometheus only.

panels.title: Operations overview
panels.description: Current values first, activity over time below, and selected-period comparisons in the expandable sections.

options.content:
### Echo Observatory · Operations
**Current state** is shown in cards and tables. Trend charts show rates or changing resource use; comparison bars cover the selected time range. Admin traffic is excluded from demand. Use **Inspect → Data** for exact values or CSV.

panels.title: Readiness
panels.description: Ready and successfully scraped targets divided by known Echo scrape targets in the selected range. Failed scrapes cannot count as ready; missing readiness samples are unavailable, never assumed healthy. See the instance table for individual states.

targets.expr: sum(echo_observatory_ready{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"} * on(job, instance) (up{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"} and on(job, instance) max_over_time(echo_observatory_ready{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__range]))) / count((up{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"} and on(job, instance) max_over_time(echo_observatory_ready{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__range])))

panels.title: Operations/s
panels.description: Completed HTTP requests, native TCP metadata sessions and gRPC calls per second. Streams count when they finish. Includes UI traffic, excludes the admin listener; not unique visitors.

panels.title: In-flight work
panels.description: HTTP handlers and gRPC calls currently running, including WebSocket and RPC session lifetimes. Raw TCP sessions and the admin listener are excluded. Not a request queue length.

panels.title: Connections
panels.description: Accepted transport connections currently open. WebSocket logical sessions are excluded to avoid counting their underlying HTTP/TLS connection twice. Admin connections are excluded.

panels.title: Egress/s
panels.description: Successfully sent socket bytes, including TLS/QUIC framing. Excludes network headers, retransmissions and infrastructure traffic; not a billing meter.

panels.title: Process RAM
panels.description: Current resident memory summed across selected Echo processes. Includes heap and other process memory, not total VM/container use. Listener selection does not apply.

panels.title: Instance status
panels.description: Latest scrape, process liveness, traffic readiness and elapsed process age per target. Uptime is a current duration, not availability. Missing values are unknown; failed scrapes may leave stale process fields briefly.

panels.title: Operations by listener
panels.description: Completed operations per second by listener. TCP metadata sessions and gRPC calls are operations, not HTTP requests. Long-lived streams appear at completion; admin excluded.

panels.title: HTTP handler latency
panels.description: Bucket-based p50/p95 estimates for HTTP handlers. Includes deliberate demo delays and unsuccessful responses; excludes admin, raw TCP, gRPC and WebSocket session duration. Not network round-trip time; sparse traffic makes estimates coarse.

panels.title: HTTP outcomes
panels.description: Completed HTTP outcomes per second. Intentional 4xx/5xx demo responses are outcomes, not proof of application failure. Requests without a final numeric status appear separately; admin excluded.

panels.title: Error events
panels.description: Recorded error events per second by type, including invalid payloads, cancellations, timeouts and internal failures. These are not all server faults. One operation can produce several events; intentional status controls and admission rejections are separate. Missing series may mean no matching event yet.

panels.title: Listener state
panels.description: Last reported running/stopped state by configured listener. Missing scrapes leave gaps. Disabled listeners are absent; H2C is the combined HTTP/1.1 + h2c server. Use Instance status to verify scrape freshness.

panels.title: HTTP routes · operations in range
panels.description: Estimated completed HTTP operations over the selected interval, adjusted for counter resets. Only HTTP listeners; native TCP and gRPC empty route labels are excluded. Top eight bounded route groups; arbitrary paths share other.

panels.title: Transport data · selected range
panels.description: Estimated bytes sent/received during the selected interval, adjusted for resets. An instant interval total, not a rolling-total time graph. Includes TLS/QUIC framing, excludes admin and some network overhead; not billed data.

panels.title: HTTP protocols · requests in range
panels.description: Estimated HTTP request counts by negotiated protocol over the selected interval. Includes UI and completed WebSocket upgrades, excludes admin. Not unique connections or visitors.

panels.title: IP families · requests in range
panels.description: Estimated HTTP request counts by observed client IP family over the selected interval. No client address labels and no unique-visitor inference. Admin excluded.

panels.title: gRPC outcomes · calls in range
panels.description: Estimated completed calls by final gRPC code over the selected interval, including Echo, health and reflection. Streams count when they end. Listener selection does not apply because these counters have no listener label.

panels.title: WebSocket messages
panels.description: Complete text/binary messages received and echoed per second; excludes control frames. Compare directions, do not add them as separate user operations. Listener selection does not apply.

panels.title: Transport throughput
panels.description: Socket bytes per second by direction across selected listeners, including TLS/QUIC framing. Curves show activity changes; the range-total bars answer how much data moved. Admin excluded; not billed traffic.

panels.title: Daily allowance
panels.description: Current budget-day state per instance, not a total for the dashboard interval. Disabled protection has zero allowance. Reservations can exceed bytes actually sent and durable reservations survive restart; each replica has its own budget, not a provider billing cap.

panels.title: Burst headroom · now
panels.description: Fraction of tokens currently available per bucket and instance. Peer buckets show the lowest headroom across groups active in the last ten minutes, never identities. Sampled current state can miss short bursts; use rejection trends too. Absent when disabled.

panels.title: Sustained rate use
panels.description: Charged tokens/second divided by configured refill for each global bucket. 100% = the sustained rate; bursts can temporarily exceed it. Egress is reserved bytes, not successfully sent or billed bytes. Not a rejection probability.

panels.title: Admission rejections
panels.description: Rejected work per second by reason, including rate, concurrency, quota and invalid connection-metadata checks. These are not all rate-limit events. Backpressure waits are excluded; one operation can generate more than one rejection event.

panels.title: Peer tracking · now
panels.description: Recently active IPv4 address/IPv6 /64 groups divided by retained-group capacity. Near capacity, LRU eviction can reset peer burst state. No identities are exported. Absent when peer limiting is disabled.

panels.title: Configured rate & burst
panels.description: Per instance and bucket. Refill/s and Burst are operations/connections for those buckets, bytes for ingress/egress. Peer limits apply per client group. Static configuration belongs in this table; use headroom/rate trends to tune it. Absent when disabled.

panels.title: Certificate validity · per instance
panels.description: Dates and remaining validity from the same instance and last observed ordinary server leaf certificate. Negative remaining time means expired. ACME challenges are excluded. These dates do not establish trust, hostname validity or future renewal success. Missing on older builds or before observation.

panels.title: Process memory
panels.description: Resident memory and live Go heap per instance. These overlap and must not be added. A trend helps find growth or leaks; neither measures the entire VM/container. Unrelated process metrics are excluded.

panels.title: Process CPU · one core = 100%
panels.description: Process CPU fraction of one core: 100% = one full core and multi-core workloads can exceed 100%. This is not the host quota, throttle time or total VM CPU.

panels.title: File descriptors · now
panels.description: Open descriptors divided by a positive process limit, where the operating system exports it. Missing/invalid limits stay unavailable rather than becoming zero use. High sustained use can indicate connection pressure or leaked files.

targets.expr: (process_open_fds{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"} and on(job, instance) max_over_time(echo_observatory_ready{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__range])) / ((process_max_fds{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"} and on(job, instance) max_over_time(echo_observatory_ready{job=~"$job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__range])) > 0)

panels.title: Dependency state
panels.description: Configured external readiness dependency: Ready or Pending/failed. Not published when no dependency is configured. Scrapes and readiness requests never initiate a new outbound check.

panels.title: Dependency checks · selected range
panels.description: Estimated actual background checks by result over the selected interval. These counts describe checks, not traffic or visitors. Absent when the feature has not produced a series.

panels.title: Dependency check latency
panels.description: Bucket-based p95 duration of actual background dependency checks, per job and instance. This trend can reveal a slow dependency. No samples when disabled or unobserved; not echo handler latency.
